photos.question: The nurse is teaching a client who is starting alendronate for osteoporosis. Which instruction is correct?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #259!

🦴 One bone medication has some very strict rules. Do you know them?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Take It with a Full Glass of Plain Water

🧠 Rationale: Alendronate must be taken first thing in the morning on an empty stomach.

A full glass of plain water helps it reach the stomach and lowers the risk of esophagus irritation.

Food, coffee and milk block absorption, and lying down can cause esophagitis.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Alendronate

💊 Drug Class: Bisphosphonate

❤️ Primary Use: Preventing and treating osteoporosis

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Heartburn and esophagus irritation

🔹 Trouble swallowing

🔹 Rare jaw bone problems

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Take in the morning before food or other meds

✅ Use 6 to 8 oz of plain water only

✅ Stay upright for at least 30 minutes

✅ Wait 30 minutes before eating

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Water, wake, wait upright 30!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: A client arrives in the ED with chest pain. Which lab result is most specific for a myocardial infarction?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #260!

❤️ Chest pain in the ED. Which lab tells you it is a heart attack?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Troponin

🧠 Rationale: Troponin is the most specific lab for damage to heart muscle.

It starts to rise within a few hours of a myocardial infarction and stays high for days.

Potassium, hemoglobin and sodium matter, but they do not confirm an MI.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Troponin and MI

❤️ What It Shows: Injury to the heart muscle

⏱️ Timing: Rises within about 3 to 4 hours and stays high up to 2 weeks

⚠️ MI Signs:

🔹 Chest pain or pressure

🔹 Pain to the jaw, arm or back

🔹 Shortness of breath and sweating

🔹 Women may have fatigue or nausea only

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Get a 12 lead ECG within 10 minutes

✅ Draw serial troponins

✅ Give oxygen if SpO2 is low

✅ Give aspirin and nitroglycerin as ordered

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Troponin tells the truth about the heart!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Cardiac #MI #CardiacNursing #Troponin #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse is suctioning a client's tracheostomy. Which action is correct?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #261!

🫁 Suctioning a trach the wrong way can drop oxygen fast. What comes first?

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Give 100% Oxygen Before Suctioning

🧠 Rationale: Suctioning removes oxygen along with secretions.

Giving 100% oxygen first helps prevent hypoxia.

Suction is applied only while pulling the catheter out, for 10 to 15 seconds at most.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Tracheostomy Suctioning

🫁 When to Suction: Only when needed, such as noisy breathing, visible secretions or low SpO2

⚠️ Watch For:

🔹 Low oxygen saturation

🔹 Bradycardia or other dysrhythmias

🔹 Airway irritation

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Use sterile technique in the hospital

✅ Hyperoxygenate before and after

✅ Suction 10 to 15 seconds per pass

✅ Rest the client between passes

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Oxygen in, suction out, 15 seconds tops!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Which Glasgow Coma Scale score indicates a severe brain injury?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #262!

🧠 One number tells you a brain injury is severe. Do you know it?

This is a HIGH-YIELD neuro question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — 7

🧠 Rationale: A GCS of 8 or less means a severe brain injury.

At this level the client may not be able to protect the airway.

A score of 15 is normal, 13 to 15 is mild and 9 to 12 is moderate.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Glasgow Coma Scale

🧠 What It Measures: Eye opening, verbal response and motor response

📊 Score Range: 3 (lowest) to 15 (normal)

⚠️ Severity:

🔹 13 to 15: mild

🔹 9 to 12: moderate

🔹 8 or less: severe

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check GCS often and trend the scores

✅ Report any drop of 2 or more points

✅ Protect the airway in low scores

🚑 Emergency: A falling GCS can mean rising ICP. Notify the provider right away.

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Less than 8, intubate!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Neuro #GlasgowComaScale #TraumaNursing #BrainInjury #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A child is receiving chemotherapy for leukemia. Which vaccine should the nurse expect to hold?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #263!

💉 Not every vaccine is safe for a child on chemo. Which one is held?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — MMR

🧠 Rationale: MMR is a live vaccine.

Live vaccines can cause infection in a child with a weak immune system.

Inactivated vaccines like the flu shot are not live and may be given per the provider.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Live Vaccines

💉 Common Live Vaccines:

🔹 MMR

🔹 Varicella

🔹 Nasal spray flu vaccine

🔹 Rotavirus

⚠️ Avoid Live Vaccines In:

🔹 Chemotherapy

🔹 High dose steroids

🔹 Pregnancy

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check immune status before any vaccine

✅ Teach family to keep up with their own vaccines

✅ Review the timing with the oncology team

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Weak immune system? No live vaccines!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: The nurse is teaching a client with chronic kidney disease about diet. Which food should the client limit?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #264!

🍌 A healthy snack can be risky for weak kidneys. Can you spot it?

This is a HIGH-YIELD renal question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Bananas

🧠 Rationale: Bananas are high in potassium.

Damaged kidneys cannot remove extra potassium well.

High potassium can cause dangerous heart rhythms.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Chronic Kidney Disease Diet

🫘 What Happens: The kidneys cannot filter waste, fluid and electrolytes well

⚠️ Foods to Limit:

🔹 High potassium: bananas, oranges, potatoes, tomatoes

🔹 High phosphorus: dairy, colas, processed foods

🔹 High sodium: canned and salty foods

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Follow fluid limits if ordered

✅ Avoid salt substitutes, which often contain potassium

✅ Take phosphate binders with meals

🚑 Emergency: Muscle weakness or an irregular heartbeat can mean high potassium.

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Bad kidneys, no bananas!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Renal #CKD #KidneyDisease #NutritionNursing #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse is monitoring a client in labor. Which fetal heart rate is within the normal range?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #265!

🤰 Do you know the normal fetal heart rate?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — 145/min

🧠 Rationale: The normal fetal heart rate baseline is 110 to 160 beats per minute.

A baseline below 110 is bradycardia.

A baseline above 160 is tachycardia.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Fetal Heart Rate

❤️ Normal Baseline: 110 to 160/min

⚠️ Abnormal Findings:

🔹 Bradycardia: under 110/min

🔹 Tachycardia: over 160/min

🔹 Late decelerations

🔹 Minimal or absent variability

🚨 Nursing Actions for Late Decels:

✅ Turn the client to her side

✅ Stop oxytocin if running

✅ Give IV fluids and oxygen as ordered

✅ Notify the provider

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

110 to 160 keeps the baby keen!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!
